knowledge:
- key_parameters: model=The name of the GSEA annotation model to download ("C2" or "PLIERpriors") ;; load=Logical indicating whether to load the model directly ;; num.out=The number of top validation results to display or return ;; swCutoff=Average silhouette width cutoff to filter RAVs (typically >= 0) ;; scoreCutoff=Validation score cutoff to filter results ;; clsizecutoff=Cluster size cutoff to filter results ;; whichPC=Specific PC from the dataset to check ;; interactive=Logical indicating whether to plot an interactive zoomable graph ;; indexOnly=Logical indicating whether to return only the indices of validated RAVs ;; studyTitle=Logical indicating whether to include study titles in the output ;; both=Logical indicating whether to print both top and bottom enriched pathways ;; n=Number of pathways to print ;; k=Number of keyword-containing pathways to filter RAVs
- alternatives: None mentioned.
- when_to_use: When a user has a new transcriptomic dataset (RNA-seq or microarray, represented as a matrix, ExpressionSet, or SummarizedExperiment with gene symbols) and wants to interpret it by comparing it to public archives without high-performance computing requirements.
- pitfalls: Input genes must be in 'symbol' format ;; The first interactive run of getModel requires user permission to create a cache directory ;; Focus should be on RAVs with higher validation scores, using average silhouette width as a secondary quality control criterion

workflows.name: transcriptomic_dataset_validation
workflows.intent: Validate a user's transcriptomic dataset against a pre-built RAVmodel to identify and biologically interpret the most relevant Replicable Axes of Variation (RAVs).
input: dataset.rds (ExpressionSet, SummarizedExperiment, or matrix containing gene expression data with gene symbols)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the GenomicSuperSignature package and download/load the pre-built RAVmodel using getModel.
2. Load the user's transcriptomic dataset (ensuring gene symbols are used).
3. Validate the dataset against the RAVmodel using validate to calculate validation scores.
4. Visualize the validation results using heatmapTable and plotValidate.
5. Extract the indices of the top validated RAVs using validatedSignatures.
6. Interpret the validated RAVs using word clouds of MeSH terms (drawWordcloud), GSEA pathway annotations (annotateRAV or subsetEnrichedPathways), and associated prior studies (findStudiesInCluster).
7. Search for specific biological themes using keyword-based queries with findSignature and findKeywordInRAV.
workflows.code:
library(GenomicSuperSignature)
library(bcellViper)
RAVmodel <- getModel("PLIERpriors", load=TRUE)
data(bcellViper)
dset
val_all <- validate(dset, RAVmodel)
head(val_all)
heatmapTable(val_all, RAVmodel, num.out = 5, swCutoff = 0)
plotValidate(val_all, interactive = FALSE)
validated_ind <- validatedSignatures(val_all, RAVmodel, num.out = 3, swCutoff = 0, indexOnly = TRUE)
validated_ind
set.seed(1)
drawWordcloud(RAVmodel, validated_ind[1])
drawWordcloud(RAVmodel, validated_ind[2])
drawWordcloud(RAVmodel, validated_ind[3])
annotateRAV(RAVmodel, validated_ind[2])
subsetEnrichedPathways(RAVmodel, validated_ind[2], include_nes = TRUE)
subsetEnrichedPathways(RAVmodel, validated_ind, include_nes = TRUE)
findSignature(RAVmodel, "Bcell")
findSignature(RAVmodel, "Bcell", k = 5)
findKeywordInRAV(RAVmodel, "Bcell", ind = 695)
subsetEnrichedPathways(RAVmodel, ind = validated_ind[2], n = 3, both = TRUE)
subsetEnrichedPathways(RAVmodel, ind = 695, n = 3, both = TRUE)
subsetEnrichedPathways(RAVmodel, ind = 953, n = 3, both = TRUE)
subsetEnrichedPathways(RAVmodel, ind = 1994, n = 3, both = TRUE)
findStudiesInCluster(RAVmodel, validated_ind[2])
findStudiesInCluster(RAVmodel, validated_ind[2], studyTitle = TRUE)
